draft.title: Withdrawal and the fall of Saigon
card: By the early 1970s the US wanted to leave Vietnam. President Nixon's policy of Vietnamisation handed more of the fighting to South Vietnam's army while US troops were reduced.
The Paris Peace Accords of January 1973 set a ceasefire. They led to the withdrawal of the remaining US troops and the return of US prisoners of war.
The agreement did not end the war between North and South Vietnam. North Vietnamese troops stayed in the South, and fighting went on.
In 1975 North Vietnam launched a major offensive. South Vietnam's army collapsed quickly, and North Vietnamese forces took Saigon in April 1975. Vietnam was later united under communist rule.
draft.remember: The US left in 1973, but the war went on until the North took Saigon in 1975.

a.q: Why did the Paris Peace Accords of 1973 not end the war in Vietnam?
opts: Fighting between North and South Vietnam continued
US troops stayed in South Vietnam to defend Saigon
North Vietnam withdrew its forces from the South
South Vietnam's army was disbanded under the terms
a.why: The Accords removed US forces but left North Vietnamese troops in the South, so the war between the two Vietnams went on. US troops did not stay, as the agreement led to their withdrawal.
a.clue: Think about who was still fighting after the US left.

b.q: A student says the fall of Saigon in 1975 happened because US troops were driven out of the city by the North. What is wrong with this claim?
opts: US troops had already left after the 1973 Accords
US troops left Saigon only after it fell in 1975
The North took Saigon with the help of US troops
Saigon was taken in 1973, before the Accords were signed
b.why: The remaining US troops left after the 1973 Accords, so the 1975 fall of Saigon was a defeat of South Vietnam's army by the North. The claim wrongly puts US troops in the city in 1975.
b.clue: Compare the date US troops left with the date Saigon fell.

a.best: Fighting between North and South Vietnam continued

b.best: US troops had already left after the 1973 Accords

problems.detail: The right option, 'Fighting between North and South Vietnam continued', only restates that the war did not end; it does not say why. The cause the card gives is that North Vietnamese troops were allowed to stay in the South. An option naming that cause would test the idea better.

The why says the claim 'wrongly puts US troops in the city in 1975'. Some US military personnel, such as embassy Marine guards and Defense Attaché Office staff, were in Saigon in April 1975 and were flown out in Operation Frequent Wind just before the city fell. The error in the claim is that the North beat South Vietnam's army, not US forces. The why should not suggest no US troops were present.
